hints.title: Partition Criteria for Finding Elements
hints.text: A number is guaranteed to be located successfully if and only if all preceding elements are strictly smaller and all following elements are strictly larger.

hints.title: Prefix Maximum and Suffix Minimum Sweeps
hints.text: Precompute running maximums from left to right, and running minimums from right to left.

hints.title: Satisfying Dual Inequality
hints.text: An index i is binary searchable if prefix_max[i] <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= suffix_min[i].

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def binarySearchableNumbers(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        suffix_min = [0] * n
        curr_min = float("inf")
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            curr_min = min(curr_min, nums[i])
            suffix_min[i] = curr_min
            
        ans = 0
        curr_max = float("-inf")
        for i in range(n):
            if curr_max < nums[i] and nums[i] <= suffix_min[i]:
                ans += 1
            curr_max = max(curr_max, nums[i])
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Two-pass prefix maximum and suffix minimum verification.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating binary search pivot paths for every target takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Prefix/suffix arrays check boundary inequalities in constant time per element.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should deduce that binary searchability requires being greater than all previous and less than all subsequent elements.
